newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistani newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistani newspapers - July 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NATION
- Pakistan successfully test fired an air-to-surface and anti-tank guided missile.
THE MUSLIM
- Senate chairman Wasim Sajjad will visit the U.S. in the second week of August.
THE NEWS
- Pakistan Law Commission finalises report on jail reforms.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto calls for revolutionary steps to rescue the country from economic crisis.
- Asian Development Bank to provide $250 million to Pakistan under its Capital Market Development programme.
DAWN
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif says his government will formulate a comprehensive action plan to solve the law and order problem in Karachi.
- Pakistan, Turkmenistan, UNOCAL of the U.S. and Delta Oil of Saudi Arabia entered into a joint agreement to construct the Turkmen-Afghanistan-Pakistan gas pipeline project by December 1998.
- Pakistan and the U.S. sign an agreement under PL-480 to offer $20 million to Islamabad for import of wheat.
- Five people killed in two separate attacks by terrorists in Vehari and Sheikhupura districts in Punjab province.
- A U.S. State Department report on religious freedom, describes Pakistan's blasphemy laws as discriminatory and demands their repeal.
- At least five people were killed and seven injured while hundreds of houses were damaged following heavy monsoon rains that lashed parts of Balochistan province.
- The Karachi stock market attracted 389.7 million rupees in foreign investment in June bringing the total flow from January to June 1997 to 4.391 billion rupees, brokerage houses said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Prime Minister Sharif said his government wanted to give constitutional protection to all long-term policies that promote investment, industrialisation and overall economic development.
- Paul Chabrier, International Monetary Fund's director for the Middle East, said talks with Pakistani leaders have been "frank, friendly and fruitful."
- Private cotton exporters have registered fresh contracts of 5,569 375-lb bales with various countries.
- Heiress Sita White who brought paternity claim against cricketer-turned politician Imran Khan, is planning to pursue her case in British courts.
- Pakistan's exports of raw cotton was 142,212 375-lb bales from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop, compared to 1.824 million bales upto July 31, 1996, the Karachi Cotton Association said.
FINANCIAL POST
- Negotiations for a three-year enhanced structural adjustment facility between Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund's visiting mission have reached the final stage.
